patch.value: Annotation transposition recovery: detect pm <collection> add <id> before the item id is consumed as text

GitHub #979 reproduces a cross-collection agent grammar mistake: noun-verb-object input is parsed as id=add and text=<real item id>, then reported as a duplicate text-source collision. The refusal must recognize the resolvable item id, name the transposed subcommand, render role-labeled recovery data, and make the accepted --note alias discoverable or reject it. Duplicate check searched all statuses for notes add, transposed subcommand, annotation collision, item-id-as-text, and --note help; closed pm-185870 owns general unknown positional subcommands but not this annotation parser collision.

When an annotation collection receives id=add and its text positional resolves to a real item, the typed SDK/CLI refusal names the transposed subcommand and supplies the canonical pm <collection> <id> --add form; the machine-readable recovery bundle labels parsed positional roles rather than flattening them; notes, learnings, files, docs, comments, and test share the behavior; the accepted --note alias is declared in help/contracts or removed with a typed migration refusal; focused unit, integration, packaged npm/npx/bun/bunx acceptance, exact 100/100/100/100 coverage, and docstring gates pass
Turn a common annotation grammar transposition into a one-turn, machine-actionable recovery
Avoid repeated failed agent turns and prevent normalized recovery receipts from obscuring positional roles
All annotation collections become safer and cheaper for agents to drive
The defect reproduces on the latest immutable 2026.8.11 package and currently affects notes, learnings, files, docs, comments, and test workflows
In a temporary workspace with item tst-y0bb, run pm notes add tst-y0bb --note hello; observe id=add/text=tst-y0bb collision guidance instead of transposed-subcommand recovery
A typed refusal says add is not an annotation subcommand, identifies tst-y0bb as the item id, and shows pm notes tst-y0bb --add hello
The CLI reports that note text was supplied twice and emits a flat normalized_args receipt that hides which token filled each positional slot
